transcript.text: Good evening, everyone. We're here for the preflight meeting on the Harborlight showcase. Before I can approve the final showcase package, I need to hear the final reports from our technical director and our music rights coordinator. Let's start with the technical director — please give us your report on the production setup, including the eight-piece live band, the 90-minute performance runtime, and any technical concerns around the audience recording permissions. Then we'll move to the music rights coordinator for the rights report, particularly on 'Neon Atlas' as our closing song. Who's ready to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical technical issue. I received the completed power survey from the Harborlight electrician this morning — the theater can safely support a live band only if it is configured as six musicians, not eight, and the electrical load plan permits a maximum performance length of 75 minutes, not 90. I haven't entered this in the production draft yet because the signed survey arrived after the draft was circulated.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to give my music rights report now. I confirmed with the publisher that 'Neon Atlas' is not cleared for this live showcase. The publisher approved 'Glass River' as the replacement closing song, and the license prohibits audience recording of the performance. I'm still waiting for the countersigned license scan before I can attach it to the show file.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you both for these critical reports. Let me make sure I have this straight before I record a decision. Rafael, you're telling us the Harborlight power survey caps us at six musicians and 75 minutes maximum — so the eight-piece band and 90-minute runtime in the current draft are not electrically feasible as written. June, you're telling us 'Neon Atlas' is not cleared, 'Glass River' is the approved replacement closing song, and the license prohibits audience recording. These are significant changes from our current draft. Before I settle the final package, I want to confirm with both of you: Rafael, can you commit to updating the production draft to reflect six musicians and 75 minutes based on the signed power survey? And June, can you commit to attaching the countersigned license once it arrives, with 'Glass River' as the closing song and audience recording prohibited? I need both commitments logged so we can proceed with an accurate final package.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Yes, Morgan, I can commit to that. I'll update the production draft to reflect six musicians and a 75-minute maximum performance length based on the signed power survey from the Harborlight electrician. I'll also make sure the audience recording permission is removed from the draft to align with June's license restriction. The updated draft will be ready for your final approval once June's countersigned license is attached.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Yes, Morgan, I can commit to that. Once I receive the countersigned license scan, I will attach it to the show file with 'Glass River' as the approved closing song and the audience recording prohibition clearly noted. I'll notify you as soon as it's in the file so Rafael can finalize the updated draft for your final approval.
